game: LAC@KC Week 6 / kickoff not in pack / KC -7.5 / total 41.5 (implied KC 24.5, LAC 17) / weather not saved

script.base: KC is a 7.5-point favorite in a 41.5 game, so the book has them up by about a TD and draining clock. Walker is the offense in the pack window: 64 carries, 364 yards (21.3 per game, 5.69 YPC) over weeks 2-4 plus 14 targets. Base flow is KC ahead by halftime, run lean, LAC chasing in the second half, Herbert dropbacks up, Hampton and Mitchell carries down, KC pass volume secondary to the run.
script.flip1: LAC stays within a score or leads, using Herbert's scramble role (16 carries, 111 yards over weeks 3-5) and the Hampton/Mitchell committee. KC then throws: Mahomes EPA/dropback is +0.42 vs blitz (n=40) and LAC blitzes 27%, so Worthy (168 air yards) and Thornton (245 air yards, not a listed prop) become the path, and Walker carries fall off 91.5.
script.flip2: KC is up big early, Walker is rested, and Emmett Johnson (8 carries, 32 yards over those three games, no targets listed) vultures the fourth quarter. LAC empties the backfield, so Hampton (38/134) and Mitchell (24/102) rush lines die while checkdowns to Mitchell (13 targets, -24 air yards) and Vidal (8 targets) rise.

injury_fallout: Pack has no injury report, practice status, questionable tags, or inactives, so no defensive starter is confirmed out and no next-man-up share can be sourced. Roles are the box-score window only. KC backfield is Walker 64/364 versus Johnson 8/32 and Tonga 2/3; a Walker limit would hand Johnson the carries, but the pack does not show that. LAC is a committee: Hampton 38/134, Mitchell 24/102, Vidal 14/88, Herbert 16/111 over weeks 3-5. Pass volume sat with Harris (16 targets, 152 yards, 182 air), not McConkey (7 targets, 66 yards, 97 air); that collapse is unexplained here, so McConkey is not bet as injured or as a healthy WR1. KC target order in-window: Kelce 17/175, Worthy 16/115, Rice 15/171, Thornton 14/219, Walker 14/66, Gray 7/56, Royals 5/17. No coverage player or pass rusher is listed out.

matchup.shell: Coverage charting is not in the pack: no MOFO/MOFC split and no man/zone rate, so WRs cannot be mapped to specific zone defenders. Only blitz rates are available: KC 28%, LAC 27%.
matchup.pressure: Herbert EPA/dropback is -0.34 vs blitz (n=44) versus -0.17 with no blitz, and KC blitzes 28%, so pressure that arrives should cut LAC deep yards (Harris 182 air, Johnston 134 air, Gadsden 116 air) and tilt LAC toward Mitchell and Vidal checkdowns. Mahomes is the opposite: +0.42 EPA vs blitz (n=40) versus +0.12 unblitzed, so LAC's 27% blitz rate feeds KC explosives rather than forcing checkdowns.
matchup.bleeds: KC pass YPA allowed: middle 8.44 on 39 att, left 6.23 on 52, right 4.96 on 53. KC rush defense 3.61 YPC, 11 runs of 10+, 11 passes of 20+ on 149 att. LAC pass YPA allowed: left 8.25 on 56 att, right 7.25 on 53, middle 5.59 on 32. LAC rush defense 4.04 YPC, 13 runs of 10+ in 5 games, 14 passes of 20+ on 152 att. LAC bleeds on the perimeter and is sound in the middle; KC bleeds in the middle, is sound on the right, and is a strong run defense.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Walker, not a receiver: primary ball carrier in a KC-lead script against a run defense that has allowed 4.04 YPC and 13 explosive runs, not a brick wall. Kelce at 58.3 yards per game runs into LAC's best zone (middle 5.59 YPA), so he is not the weak-spot overlap. Worthy and Thornton air yards overlap LAC's left/right bleed and the blitz-EPA edge, but that needs the pass-heavy flip, not the base script. LAC's listed primary, Harris, is not in the available props. Hampton's 3.53 YPC runs into KC's 3.61 YPC rush defense, a bad overlap for an LAC rush over.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Walker is the KC offense in a clock-control favorite script, 21 carries and 121 rush yards a game in the last three listed, and 91.5 still sits about 30 yards under that role against a defense that has allowed 4.04 YPC and 13 runs of 10+.
edge_players.must_be_true: Walker plays a full lead-back share, KC is ahead or close enough to keep handing him the ball, and he stays near 18-plus carries. Health is inferred only from the weeks 2-4 workload; the pack has no final injury report.
edge_players.kills_it: Blowout rest (flip 2) caps him around 12-14 carries, or LAC leads and KC abandons the run (flip 1), or 5.69 YPC regresses toward LAC's 4.04 allowed rate on a 20-carry day (about 81-86 yards). The missing week 5 could also be a hidden snap limit.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Johnson is an 8-carry, 32-yard backup over three games with no targets listed, and 24.5 rush-plus-rec yards is a real workload he does not get while Walker is the clock-control back in a one-score KC lead.
edge_players.must_be_true: Walker is active and keeps early-down and goal-line work, the game does not become extended garbage time, and Johnson's receiving share stays near zero as in the pack window.
edge_players.kills_it: Script-dependent: a KC blowout that sits Walker, a Walker in-game injury the pack cannot flag, or a long fourth-quarter series of 6-8 carries pushes him through 24.5. Flip 2 kills this leg.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot price a true edge or size a rung. Form agrees with both leans: Walker 121 rush yards per game vs 91.5, Johnson about 10.7 rush yards and 0 listed receiving vs 24.5 rush-plus-rec. That is form agreement, not a model probability; neither leg is treated as 70%+. Juice is modest (Walker over -116.5, Johnson under -120), not a short alt. Caveat for the human, not a sim disagreement and not a cut: 21 carries times LAC's 4.04 YPC is about 86, under 91.5, so efficiency regression can still lose the Walker over. Nothing in the pack contradicts the Johnson usage under in the base script.

market_rung_price: Walker rush yards over 91.5 at -116.5. Rush yards, not rush-plus-rec 117.5 at -115, because the edge is carry share in a positive script, and 117.5 also needs his 22 receiving yards per game on top of a rush total that may regress. Johnson rush-plus-rec under 24.5 at -120 rather than rush under 13.5 at -113, because 13.5 is only a few yards above his 10.7 rush average and one series busts it, while 24.5 still loses only if he gets a real blowout workload. No alt rungs and no no-vig in the pack.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because KC led big by half, Walker had about 13 carries in the 60s before sitting, and the 5.69 YPC never showed up against a front allowing 4.04 YPC, so he finished under 91.5, while Johnson ran 8 or 9 times in the fourth and cleared 24.5. The other loss path is flip 1: LAC led, Mahomes threw into a 27% blitz he has crushed at +0.42 EPA, Walker never saw 18 carries, and the clock-control story was the wrong script. A hidden week-5 injury or a late inactive, neither in this pack, would have made both legs unplayable.
slip_story: One story: KC leads a moderate 41.5 game and runs the clock. Walker rush-yards over is the anchor; Johnson rush-plus-rec under belongs because that same script keeps the ball with the starter. Do not add LAC RB overs (Hampton 44.7, Mitchell 34, Vidal 29 all sit above their rush lines but die if the dog abandons the run), and do not add Worthy or Kelce overs, which need the pass-heavy flip (Worthy 38.3 vs 49; Kelce into a 5.59 middle). Do not add McConkey or Royals unders just because 42.5 and 24.5 sit far above three-game yards; those gaps are unexplained news. No TDs, no receptions, no passing yards. Two legs, not a forced third, because no other same-script prop in the list survives the pre-mortem.
